title: Ernesto, Larry, Freddie the Freeloader and Crip

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Studio work and jingles: New York session life

blocks.x: who used to carry around musical instruments all the time.
Crib?
No, Ernesto.

Ernesto, yes. He was amazing. He was one of those wiry Italian guys. I think he was originally -- I think he had a shoeshine stand. And one of the guys used to leave his instruments by the shoeshine stand, I think it was Stanley Webb, or somebody like that, would leave them there. Then Ernesto would say, you know the bother I take for you, or something like that. And he just wound up packing everybody's instruments around for them.
(Inaudible).
About five feet tall and he could carry something like 600 pounds of instruments at one time.
Two drums, wheeling down the street.
Anytime, 24 hours a day, never complained. I don't know how he did it.
Amazing. You call him any hour of the night, 2:00 o'clock in the morning, and tell him you had a date at RCA --
He never goofed.
Never wrote it down. I don't think he could write. And never goofed.
No, that's right, he never wrote anything down. That's right.
You remember that guy Larry, he tried to horn in? Yeah.
He only had one problem, he didn't deliver the instruments, he'd steal them. You used to go into a recording date and he'd walk out with four overcoats on.
(Laughter.)
And then we had Freddie the Freeloader.
Oh, Freddie the Freeloader. You know, he got famous, they made a record called "Freddie the Freeloader."
Yeah. He would come to a date and he used to sit there while we were recording. And if you looked over, he'd be nodding. Record's going to be a hit. Freddie's asleep.
(Laughter.)
You get some of the most beautiful/unforgettable characters in that recording business.
I'm trying to think what I knew -- you remember Crip used to come around.
Charlie Shaver's man?
Yeah, that's who it was. But after Charlie died he used to come around. I'd see him every once in a while because he always kind of liked me.
Yeah, he used to hang around 8th Avenue quite a bit. I haven't seen him recently.
